is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. gambiae s.s., An. coluzzii, An. arabiensis) in Benin.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F) and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) in Tables 1, 2, 3, and 4.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 1, 2, 3, and 4 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) and sample sizes for each population.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in the Atacora department, Benin.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is provided for specific districts: Boukoumbé, Péhunco, and Toucountouna.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study defines three distinct collection periods: 2010 (before IRS), 2016 (during IRS), and 2020 (4 years after IRS withdrawal).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections conducted in 2010, 2016, and 2020.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study analyzed the frequency of kdr (L1014F) and ace-1 (G119S) mutations in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations in three districts of the Atacora department, Benin, across three time points: before IRS (2010), during IRS (2016), and 4 years after IRS withdrawal (2020). The study found that L1014F frequency increased over time, while G119S frequency increased during IRS and reverted to pre-IRS levels after withdrawal.
